rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Berkeley landlords may not ask about, require disclosure of, or use your criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection, rent or deposit amounts, or decisions to evict or add family members. If a landlord takes action against you based on criminal history (where an exemption allows it), they must give you written notice and a chance to respond, and you can file a complaint with the Rent Board.
rules.key_value: No criminal history inquiries; fines $1,000–$10,000 per violation

coverage.summary: Rental housing in Berkeley, with exemptions for owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives on site, limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8, lifetime sex offender registrants, units rented under owner move-back agreements, and existing tenants subletting or adding roommates.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Units under owner move-back rental agreements per BMC 13.76.130 A.9
Existing tenants subletting or adding/replacing roommates

rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record resides as primary residence; units under owner move-back agreements (BMC 13.76.130 A.9); units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

notes: Official Rent Board overview of BMC 13.106, passed by City Council April 14, 2020; the page does not state an effective date. The document also mentions a written notice and opportunity-to-respond requirement and a notice-posting requirement, which are folded into the single screening restriction record.
